events.text: User review feedback: the visual wall-end tab still protruded in the live view. The first pass kept an exposed-face miter extension; that still read as crossing. Rework expected: no visible wall skin should extend past the authored endpoint.

Tightened the wall-end visual fix after review feedback. The shared hmsc-int piece shape decomposition now clamps every decorative front/back wall skin at the authored endpoint whenever the core band extends for a join; no exposed-face miter extension remains, so visible wall skins cannot leave a tab or cross past the end. The collision/core band still extends through L/T wall joins, preserving the existing blocker closure. Expanded wallSlabs regression coverage to assert both walls in an L-corner and the stem in a T-junction have no visible endpoint tabs, plus reran placed, snap, and compile parity suites.
User review feedback: still crossing. Root cause was the rendered wall core/end-cap strip also using the extended join band; previous rework only clamped the front/back face slabs.

Fixed the remaining wall-end crossing by clamping every rendered wall box, including the core/end-cap strip, to the authored wall endpoint when the gameplay/collision band extends through a join. Collision math remains unchanged and is still covered by placed tests; only the shared visual decomposition now hides the join extension. Updated wallSlabs regression coverage so L-corner and T-junction rendered cores plus front/back skins all fail if any visible endpoint tab returns. Reran wallSlabs, placed, snap, and compile world parity suites.

resolution: Fixed the wall-end visual crossing in the shared hmsc-int piece shape decomposition. The wall core still extends through perpendicular joins for collision closure, but front/back decorative slabs now clamp at the authored endpoint on joined sides; only the exposed outside face keeps the tiny miter extension. Added a focused wallSlabs regression suite covering L-corners and T-junctions, and verified the existing placed/snap/compile parity paths.
